items.note: 1889, Larrow Green and the 1891 creamery are given, but Gideon Vose (a bolded element) is never named in Section A.

Story 1: Article VII pays by butterfat as determined by test, not by weight of milk; 'whole valley's milk payment depended on the fat test taken at Ostrey Hollow' covers the station-test-governs clause.
Only says the rule was 'the crucial hinge'. Never says that under payment by weight the fault would have cost nobody anything.
Loomis, Teague and Sill are not named in Section A.
Selby Vose is named as manager, but Section A never says he was Gideon's son or that he became manager in 1913.
The station-gain ledger line does not appear in Section A.
Story 1: skimming station seven miles upstream, opened May 4 1896, glass borrowed from Larrow Green.

Core mechanism is present across Stories 1 and 7: milk weighed, a sample tested, cream sent down and skim returned; a short charge in a bottle graduated for the full charge reads low. It does not say 'composite'. Credited on the core-fact rule.
Ammon & Sons, Tarnet, invoice April 14 1897, in use May 1 1897.
6 dozen pipettes marked 17.6 cc, 12 dozen bottles, acid measure, hand tester, freight, $77.93.
Story 2: '0.19 points low in every month, every season, wet years and dry' (though it is framed as the Hollow-vs-Green gap; that is penalized at A4.3).
Never says a pipette cannot be checked without a burette or that the county had no burette.
Born 1861, 29 seasons from 1896, dismissed April 30 1925, died 1934.
The test book's columns and its crossed-and-initialed corrections are not described.
No summary leaf. The 1896 average of 3.80 is never given in Section A. Both figures are required.
Story 4: broke May 8, borrowed measure until July 10, nine weeks, tests rose then fell back, question mark. The 3.80/3.61 levels are missing. Credited on the core-fact rule (no REQUIRED line).
Married to Orra Brant, sister of Emmet Brant, the largest patron; the irony is noted.
The 1919 circular is present, but Keddie's 17 March 1925 statement (tested as taught, cannot say why, took no cream) is absent.
Story 6: lived until 1934 under the imputation. The test book's impoundment and its 1959 transfer are missing; credited on the core fact.
Hessel Bottom and Brant as largest are named, but 'six farms' on the Bottom is not stated.
The weigh book appears only as an exhibit: no 1 Jan 1897 start and no agreement of the scales.
Lost under the gate: Story 2 gives 3.61 vs 3.78 and calls the Ostrey deficiency 0.19 (it is 0.17), conflating the visible gap with the true shortfall. C1 and D3 repeat this.
The 1908 committee is mentioned without Nyle Grigg and without the Jan-Mar sampling.
Brant's 1910 year is not in Section A.
Roy Brant, the 1958 loan and Hazel are not in Section A.
Alder Corners is absent from the entire sheet.
Absent.
Absent.
Absent.
Absent.
Rosalie Cudd is absent.
Strawn is named as inspector on the Ordell circuit, but the 1907-1936 span is absent and the sheet asserts 'from 1908 forward' (NT-23).
Story 3: tested with a lactometer and never once found added water.
Story 5: June 12 1923, calibrated burette, condemned the entire lot.
Says only that he 'drew no inference'. The bolded 'wrote no figure / made no report beyond the condemnation' is not stated.
The order and ack dates are right, but the 1924 average is given as 3.85, a planted value, so the item is lost.
The crate is in the loft, but the notebooks going to the college library in 1947 is missing; both bolded elements are required.
Story 6: patrons petitioned in January 1925.
Dates, three sittings and the weigh room are given, but Alonzo Frick is never named.
Three theories aired (water, cream theft by tester, hay) and no cause established.
The four books are listed, but it is never said that Strawn's 1923 notebook contained the answer (the condemnation) and was read for its other lines.
Dismissed April 30 1925 with no cause found; award May 4 of $3,800 'without admission', charged to the station account.
No one-fifth of $19,000 and no link to the station-gain account; the sheet uses $19,600.
Ansel's granddaughter, graduate student at the State Agricultural College at Farland, co-author with Leland Vaught.
Does not say she assembled records that had never been in the same room.
February 1958, loft, nine pipettes survived. The 'of the sixty' wording takes a deduction separately.
Gives 16.27 cc, short 1.33 cc (NT-1).
No 95 percent and no 3.61-for-3.80; uses 7.5%.
$19,600, and there is no 76,000 lb or ledger identity in Section A.
Bulletin No. 471, October 1958, cleared him 24 years after death and 33 after dismissal; Story 5 has the crate sitting 35 years.
Granddaughter.
Duncan's daughter, and Duncan is Ansel's son.
Second cousins, with the correct derivation through Emmet and Orra, Roy and Duncan.
Full vs half siblings is never raised; no statement that it cannot be determined. It asserts neither, so no -2.
Gideon Vose.
Gideon drafted Article VII (pay by fat, not weight); Selby inherited that structure and circulated the watering accusation.

Borderline. 'The sources conflict ... if a connection existed, it is not established by the sources.' There is no verdict sentence saying they were not kin, so this is scored as an abstention and takes no -2.
Treats the family member's denial as outweighing the other account, which contradicts the key's 'a denial is not a record'; the established position is not stated correctly.
Takes 67,000 lb as authoritative over its own 76,000 cross-check.
Says it cannot be determined; gives no 6,840 lb.
No 360 lb.
No $86.40; gives an illustrative $33.
1,368,190 lb (treats the gain as shrinkage), not 1,520,000.
75,810 lb at 5.25%/5.53%; wrong difference and percentages.
72 is correct but the shortfall is given as 1.33 cc, not 0.88.
26 years and about 6 weeks; 25 full delivery years; partial first and last seasons excluded.
Asserts 'approximately 1.1 million pounds' (Kyle's memory) as the answer instead of abstaining.
Variable: the measuring glass, the station's own replaced by a borrowed one.
Tester, herds, season/pasture and machinery held constant.
Only 'rose markedly ... fell back'. The result figures 3.80 and 3.61 are not given.
Establishes the glass, not milk, herds, tester or hay; states limits (onset, borrowed glass's own accuracy).
Only the 1911 interval is valid. The station-gain reason is misread as shrinkage, not 'cream arrived heavy', and the equipment-source reason does not bear on theft.
It asserts independence and names the 1911 interval as surviving without 1958, but the reasons being called independent are mostly invalid.
Asserts the bookkeeper 'did not question the entries' (and misidentifies Kyle as bookkeeper).
Yes, he knew the station tested low; cites the 1919 circular.

Only two of five: he signed the ledger sheets carrying the gain line, and he wrote the 1919 circular. The manager date is wrong (1911), and neither 'never names the glassware' nor 'argued watering at the hearing' appears in B-G. Three are required.
Declines on the cause ('cannot be determined'), so no -2. But it offers only one supporting observation (signature vs reading, via Kyle's thumb on the totals); two are required.

$3,500 vs $3,800 (r21 vs r22) resolved by official record over oral memory; first cousin once removed vs second cousins resolved by derivation. No keyed E-a table row is found (it says the circular reached nine families while quoting 'eleven', and declares no contradiction).
NT-18: identifies r19 and r22 both carrying great-niece; tie broken by r22's own correction plus r18.
No abstention conflict (A04, A06, A10) is declared unsettleable; A04 is instead asserted in F.
Cites only Falke's deliberate appended correction, which is not a listed self-refutation and is already used for E-b.
Cause given as 16.27 cc, 7.57%, and a 1924 level of 3.85. No 0.95 and no 0.19 = 5% of 3.80.
Watering (Vose) defeated by Strawn's lactometer never finding water.
Theft defeated by the 1911 interval with the same man at the bench.
Bog hay defeated by Bulletin 214: five hundredths in winter, nothing in summer, against 0.19 every month.
Verdict sentence 'No.': asserts the board did not examine the glassware.
'Believed he did not know, or kept his belief private' does not declare the question undeterminable or give the son vs chairman poles. It asserts neither pole, so no -2.
About 186 words, over the 150 limit.
At most two record series are identifiable (invoice implicitly, 1958 measurement).
Contains 16.27 and $19,600.
Only three of six elements (1897, 1958, both names). No one-in-twenty, no 76,000/$19,000, no 1923 condemnation.
